clue.text: Train routes run across sea out of south-east – this?

definitions.text: Train routes run across sea out of south-east – this?

indicators.note: to train something is to shape or direct it, so the following letters are reworked into a fresh order
taking something out of a word means its letters are removed, leaving the remainder behind

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a run
the word sea with S and E, the compass abbreviation for south-east, taken away

explanation.surface: A question about which train runs across the sea from south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the Channel Tunnel service, though strictly the train goes under the sea rather than across it, so this is a near all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Channel Tunnel passenger service carries travellers from London in the south-east under the Channel to France and Belgium.

clue.text: Open Jug lifted in Faldo’s penultimate year

indicators.note: penultimate means last but one, so only the second-to-last letter of the name is kept
in a down clue, lifting a word raises it upward so that it reads from bottom to top
one piece sits in the middle of the others, which wrap around it on both sides

blocks.note: the golfer's surname, of which the last-but-one letter is kept
an olpe is an ancient Greek jug with a spout
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A golf story: the Open trophy, the Claret Jug, lifted by Nick Faldo in his second-to-last winning year.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sells the Open championship and its Claret Jug; in fact Open is a verb and the jug is an obscure Greek vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy something like a parachute or sail is to spread it out or unfurl it, a verb sense close to opening.

clue.text: Troublesome partner once buried by tax chits?

indicators.note: something buried by other material is covered over and sits inside it

blocks.note: VAT, value added tax, is the UK sales tax
a former partner is an ex
IOUs are written promises to pay, chits for debts

explanation.surface: A former partner swamped by tax demands and unpaid notes is causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vexatious causes annoyance or worry, which is a direct synonym of being bothersome and irritating.

clue.text: Ear-bone being analysed, pathologist’s left gaps

indicators.note: something being analysed is broken down and taken apart, so its letters are rearranged
here left is the past tense of leave, so the named letters depart and are removed

blocks.note: the word taken as written, without the possessive
these four letters are the ones that leave

explanation.surface: A pathologist examining an ear bone leaves gaps in the analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, A, G and S from PATHOLOGIST and seven letters remain to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An otolith is a tiny calcium carbonate structure in the inner ear of vertebrates, often called an ear stone.

clue.text: Film artistic pair receiving degree from medical school

indicators.note: something receiving another thing takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a pair of performers is a duo
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree

explanation.surface: A pair of artists at medical school gets a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is the 1941 Disney animated feature about a baby elephant with enormous ears who learns to fly.

clue.text: Superman’s trademark luck is out with Red “S” spurned by editor

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or out of place, so they are rearranged
to spurn is to reject, so the named letters are thrown out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word red followed by the letter S
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor; these letters are rejected

explanation.surface: Superman's luck runs out when an editor turns down his red S emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The red S on his chest looks like his trademark; the real trademark is the curl on his forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Superman is drawn with a small lock of hair curled flat on his forehead, a styling known as a kiss curl.

clue.text: Serpent and Fury rise up toweringly

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
ire is anger or fury

explanation.surface: A snake rears up in fury, towering over its victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspire has an archaic literal sense of rising high or soaring upward, like a spire reaching to the sky.

clue.text: This is nothing odd in fraudster

definitions.text: This is nothing odd in fraudster

indicators.note: keeping nothing from the odd positions leaves only the letters in even places

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A trick is perfectly normal behaviour for a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a con trick is nothing unusual for a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a deceptive trick or stratagem, exactly the kind of scheme a swindler routinely employs.

clue.text: I like males this way with cycling spirit

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so letters from the front are carried round to the back

blocks.note: taken as written
like and as both mean in the manner of
men are males
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: Someone who likes men to go cycling, sharing their spirited approach.
explanation.walkthrough: IASMENTHUS has its first four letters moved round to the end to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit in the sense of eager energy and keenness is a common synonym for zeal and passion.

clue.text: “Sausage?”: here!; “Spring?”: present!; “Swiss?” …

blocks.note: surface reading: a nonsense list of questions and exclamations about food and seasons
setter's reading: names are being called out and answered, each name being a kind of roll — sausage, spring, Swiss

explanation.walkthrough: Each called name pairs with roll: sausage roll, spring roll, Swiss roll; the replies here and present are what pupils say when names are read out.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is read aloud and each person answers here or present, the classroom attendance check.

clue.text: British occupying correspondingly backward area where Ottomans ruled

indicators.note: going backward means the expression is read from right to left

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
occupying gives IN and correspondingly gives SO, an expression read together
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: British forces occupying an area, with the Ottomans' former territory mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: British occupying looks like a container, but B simply comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan territory was part of the Ottoman Empire from the fifteenth century until Austro-Hungarian occupation in 1878.

clue.text: Small bank initially splits funds, setting aside 2K

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is used
a letter that splits something goes in between, dividing it into two parts
setting things aside removes them, so the named letters are dropped

blocks.note: the first letter
a kitty is a pool of money, and funds is plural, so two of them
two letter Ks, the ones set aside

explanation.surface: A small bank divides its funds after setting aside two thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 2K looks like two thousand; here it means two letter Ks, one from the front of each kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: Itty-bitty is an informal, childlike reduplicated word meaning tiny or very little.

clue.text: Half-hearted person taking meal of exceptional quality

indicators.note: half-hearted means half of the middle is lost, so one central letter of a doubled pair goes

blocks.note: one who sups, that is takes a meal, could be called a supper

explanation.surface: A diner who is only half-hearted about the meal in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of SUPPER is PP; halving it leaves a single P.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is an informal adjective meaning excellent or first-rate, describing something outstandingly good.

clue.text: Ornamental shrub reported by London park warden

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the phrase matters

blocks.note: Hyde Park is a large London park, and a ranger is a park warden

explanation.surface: A shrub mentioned by a keeper in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is one of London's royal parks, looked after by park rangers; the non-rhotic British pronunciation makes ranger and -rangea match.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrangeas are flowering garden bushes with large rounded heads of blue, pink or white blooms.

clue.text: Naked reviewer consumed, it’s implied, rare form of H

indicators.note: something naked is stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed
whatever is consumed ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a critic reviews books, plays or films
the stomach is not named but is implied by consuming, as food goes into the tummy

explanation.surface: A naked reviewer is swallowed up, with a rare element hinted at.
explanation.walkthrough: TUM, informal for stomach, is never stated: consumed implies the reviewer goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tritium is the radioactive isotope of hydrogen with two neutrons, naturally very scarce, so a rare variety of H.

clue.text: Salt barely covered herb

blocks.note: a salt and a tar are both old names for a sailor
wearing just a rag is to be barely covered: rag on

explanation.surface: Salt only just sprinkled over a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt looks like seasoning beside a herb; it is the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic culinary plant with anise-flavoured leaves, used in French cooking and béarnaise.

clue.text: Athlete heard catalogue of shrink’s patients?

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a shrink is a psychiatrist, so a roll of patients is a psych list

explanation.surface: A sports figure overhears a reading of a psychiatrist's list of clients.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrink is informal for a psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitive rider in road or track racing is a sportsperson, so an example of an athlete.

clue.text: They covered mail working together, a cos and Truss (only one succeeded)

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and moved about into a new order
only one of the two letters standing for succeeded survives, so the other is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political tale of Truss and others working together, where only one got the top job.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the abbreviation for succeeded; Truss has two, and only one is kept. Liz Truss was briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Surcoats were loose tunics worn by knights over their chain armour, so these garments covered mail.

clue.text: Avoiding the rush-hour, like yodellers yodelling?

blocks.note: first meaning: at a quieter time when travel is cheaper
second meaning, cryptic: yodellers call out from a mountain top

explanation.surface: Travelling outside busy times, compared to Alpine singers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words for the cryptic half: yodelling is done from a summit, sending the sound away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickets and journeys outside the busiest commuting periods are described as off-peak, a fixed travel term.

clue.text: Musical arrangement close to his heart

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: the final letter
the heart of something is its core

explanation.surface: A piece of music that is very dear to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Close to his heart reads as a fond phrase; close is the end of his.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written version of a composition showing every part, an orchestration or setting for instruments.

clue.text: Loud kid’s toy may set about dog with waggly tail

indicators.note: a waggly tail swings back and forth, so the end letters switch round
to be set about something is to be placed around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: may and can both express permission
a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A noisy toy may make a dog with a wagging tail jump.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail of the dog is its last two letters, swapped round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap gun is a toy pistol that fires small explosive paper caps with a sharp bang.

clue.text: Keep cutting oxygenated gas current, more conclusively

indicators.note: something cutting into a word slices through it and sits inside

blocks.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle
air is a mixture of gases
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, put into the gas
I is the symbol for electrical current

explanation.surface: Keep cutting the oxygen-rich gas supply, more firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: O, the symbol for oxygen, goes into AIR to give AIOR, which FORT then cuts after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means with even stronger reason, used when one argument follows still more certainly from another.

clue.text: Nursemaid engrossed in moderately religious book

indicators.note: someone engrossed in something is absorbed within it, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: -ish as a word means somewhat or to a moderate degree
an aia (ayah) is an Indian nursemaid

explanation.surface: A nanny absorbed in a book of mildly religious content.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is one of the major prophetic books of the Old Testament in the Bible.

clue.text: Delightful Greek valley is leaving couple a walk in the park

indicators.note: letters that are leaving depart from the word and are removed

blocks.note: a couple in a relationship is an item
something easy as pie is a walk in the park
read as the plural of I: two letter Is, which leave

explanation.surface: A lovely Greek valley is a stroll in the park for a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Is is read as Is, the plural of the letter I; both Is come out of ITEMPIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe in Thessaly was celebrated by ancient poets for its beauty, so its name came to stand for any lovely vale.

clue.text: Bit of advice one ignored near the end, something stiffening joints

indicators.note: a letter that is ignored is left out, so it is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a tip is a piece of advice
I is the Roman numeral for one; this is the letter dropped
late means near the end of a period

explanation.surface: Advice ignored towards the end, while something makes the joints stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: Stiffening joints suggests arthritis; here it is carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-shaped metal bracket is screwed across woodwork to strengthen a corner or junction between two pieces of timber.

clue.text: Restrict graffito to military building

blocks.note: to pen is to confine or restrict
a tag is a graffiti artist's signature
to and on can both mean towards or against, as in put the lid to or on

explanation.surface: Keeping graffiti confined at a military headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided headquarters of the US Department of Defense in Arlington, Virginia, houses the armed forces' leadership.

clue.text: Tactless perhaps of couple at dances

indicators.note: the letters dance about, moving into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A couple behaving tactlessly at dances.
explanation.walkthrough: Perhaps marks tactless as one example: a tactless remark is inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactless comment is inappropriate or unsuitable for the situation, one instance of something improper.

clue.text: Disagreeing with politician ticking boxes

indicators.note: the phrase boxes up the letters, holding them inside across the word break

blocks.note: found inside, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Disagreeing with a politician who ticks boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ticking boxes is a stock phrase, but boxes is the verb: politician ticking contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti works as a preposition meaning opposed to or against, so it substitutes for being against.
